review_notes: Source-first scope: the abstract and introduction frame one principal question—how low financial reporting quality changes lenders’ trade-off between accounting-based and non-accounting-based monitoring terms. The within-sample design and main results test this across the primary contractual outcomes: financial covenants, price, security, general covenants, maturity, and financial-ratio performance pricing. Retain Table 3 col. 1, Table 4 col. 1, Table 5 cols. 1–3, and Table 6 col. 1. The general-covenant and maturity models are explicitly design tests of substitute monitoring mechanisms. Exclude relationship-lender interactions, ICW-severity interactions, restatement comparisons, difference-in-differences, simultaneous-equation/SUR fits, and other robustness analyses as later moderation, comparison, endogeneity, or robustness designs.

Table 5 RHS inventory was checked against the rendered PDF page 17 because the extracted table text did not preserve all column positions. Financial Covenants appears in column 3 (maturity) only; it is not an RHS term in column 2 (general covenants).

Method remains unknown for the Table 3 and Table 4 primary regressions and Table 5 cols. 2–3. The authors print linear specifications and label the analyses regressions, but do not name those primary estimators. Poisson models are described for the separate restatement comparison and as untabulated re-estimates of covenant models. Probit is explicitly reported for Table 5 col. 1 and Table 6 col. 1.
